On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

- $x\in (-3,-1]$
- $x\in [-1,3]$
- $x\in [0,1]$
feedback.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The given function is invertible on the intervals $x\in (-3,-1]$ and on $x\in [0,1].$  Indeed, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/0388335095ed530ce07d278f82be5eb3bff14859db64b6e9ec47da27861bb657.png)

    

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval. $x\in [-1,3]$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/522b5661aaf9b7640c305b8cefd06f49cc8eed590f3ae736fc6720e6165bc3a9.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
